opening_message:
Ticket 1: Donna Ball (employee ID E024) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E024.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Donna Ball (E024) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write access (admin requires owning role; Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code), so write is within policy.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Donna Ball (E024) is a contractor with basic security training (noting a conflict with the earlier note listing full_time). Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training (never admin). Basic training means write is above the maximum, so recommend read for Source Code.
reason: Donna Ball (E024) requests write access to Source Code. The HR note lists her as full_time, but the Security agent verified in the Security DB that she is a contractor with basic security training and explicitly flagged this conflict with the HR note. Under the access policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training (never admin). With basic training, write is above the maximum, so the maximum for Source Code is read. Granting the maximum (read) since the requested level is above it.
